children: Australia's southern states are expected to face a 64-petajoule gas shortfall during the April-September 2027 winter period, increasing their reliance on supplies from Queensland and gas storage, the competition regulator said on Friday.
The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) said local production in the southern states was expected to fall short of demand during the period
Australia's southern states are expected to have enough gas in the first quarter of 2027, though some additional supply may be needed in February, the regulator said in its latest gas inquiry report

The report comes as the government advances plans to require LNG exporters to reserve part of their production for domestic users in a bid to boost supply on the east coast, where production from southern fields has declined in recent years
"Replenishing storage facilities in the early months of next year will remain important for maintaining reliable supply during periods of higher demand," ACCC Commissioner Anna Brakey said
The regulator said wholesale gas prices on Australia's east coast appeared largely unaffected by higher international prices, with most new supply deals signed between April and June at fixed prices
The ACCC's next gas inquiry report is due in December
